SP-C1.name: DVR/PID module structure and Smith bases
SP-C1.statement_used: Finite torsion-free modules over a DVR are free; finite modules decompose into free and cyclic torsion parts; full-rank submodules admit Smith bases and determinant gives their index.
SP-C1.source: Keith Conrad, Modules over a PID, Corollary2.6, Theorem4.1, Section4 aligned bases and Theorem5.22.
SP-C1.matching: Applied only to finite O modules whose finiteness is proved in the chapter. SP1 handles additive, not assumed O-linear, injections through finite cardinality. SP6 proves the norm-weighted length formula from these finite module facts.

SP-C2.name: Noetherian prime filtration
SP-C2.statement_used: A finite module over a Noetherian ring has a finite filtration with quotients R/p; the graded refinement is obtained by choosing homogeneous annihilators.
SP-C2.matching: SP2 explains the homogeneous refinement and proves the specific Euler nonnegativity argument; no positivity theorem is left as an unexplained citation.

SP-C3.name: Nullstellensatz, Nakayama and finite etale algebras over a field
SP-C3.statement_used: Maximal residue fields of finite-type algebras over algebraically closed K equal K; radical ideals are intersections of maximal ideals. For a finite local module M=mM implies M=0. Finite etale field algebras are finite products of finite separable extensions.
SP-C3.matching: SP3 base changes the nonzero finite-type algebra ((A/J_epsilon) tensor_B Frac(B/p))[1/q], never an arbitrary transcendental residue field. SP4 uses zero cotangent at all closed points and characteristic zero to prove the finite-etale slice, then gives an explicit double cover.

SP-C4.name: Bertrand prime theorem
SP-C4.statement_used: For n>1 there is a prime n<p<2n.
SP-C4.source: P.Erdos, Beweis eines Satzes von Tschebyschef, ActaSciMath(Szeged)5(1932),194-198.
SP-C4.matching: Applied at n=ell*h.N*p1+5; yields source pZero<=2ell*h.N*p1+10, with p>=5, p not dividing level or D.S.

SP-C5.kind: matched elementary local and cyclotomic number theory
SP-C5.name: Unramified Frobenius and cyclotomic value
SP-C5.statement_used: At a finite rational prime p the decomposition group modulo inertia is procyclic, generated by arithmetic Frobenius; roots of unity of order prime to p are unramified and Frobenius acts by the p-th power.
SP-C5.source: J.S.Milne, AlgebraicNumberTheory,v3.08(2020), Chapters6 and8 (cyclotomic extensions, decomposition/inertia and Frobenius); original-place transport also established in KB6.
SP-C5.matching: SP7 retains all original valuation subrings in UnrT; SP10 uses arithmetic Frobenius chi(Fr)=p, and computes H1_unr(E/O(theta)) directly as (E/O)/(theta(Fr)-1)(E/O), hence zero for finite character times a strictly negative twist.
